protocol.scope: Desktop browser performance retry after unrelated build completed; current branch bundle and verified ce7 rehearsal guest archive. Does not accept release budgets or physical devices.
protocol.comparison: Within each fresh browser process alternate LuaJIT and legacy Lua 5.1 backends; no claim of improvement against older busy-host measurements.
workloads: 3 modeled 10 Mbps cold/cached delivery pairs in separate Chromium processes
3 fresh-process Chromium rounds for small/large edits and hover
3 fresh-process Chromium rounds for imported scoreboard check/compile/hover
1 fresh Chromium process family per backend for footprint
protocol.correctness: Existing harnesses reject error diagnostics and runtime page errors; imported harness requires current edited output, hover type, and identical complete invalid-call diagnostics.
protocol.timingQualification: Process sampler records all foreign compiler processes once per second. Keep all observations; any compiler overlap invalidates a quiet-host label. Per-run percentiles are samples, not confidence intervals.

sampling.method: Once-per-second ps snapshot, process names and CPU. No competing compiler activity means no foreign compiler process at >=1% CPU was sampled; this does not establish an entirely idle host or detect every subsecond job. Raw snapshots remain in the local evidence directory.

assetsScope: Current f697aae5 browser bundle built using the verified extracted ce7 rehearsal archive. Guest build key 25ac4dcdb02ba761641be35ce90b9c40f8bd1dc6d4c61f0b3e65aed1f073be87. This is not a new guest build or a measurement of newer main.

compiler.scope: Production compiler workers; alternating backend order across fresh browser contexts; 30 samples after 3 warmups per request kind; edits change every request; host performance.now round trip. Large edit is a 2048-element literal, not a large project import.

imported.scope: Production retained compiler workers: changing application edits with six bundled-library imports. Browser memoryOnly sessions accept one source and lazily check bundled modules; they cannot load arbitrary project files. This is not a multi-file incremental-project benchmark, UI responsiveness budget, physical mobile test, or network-delivery measurement.
imported.timing: Page performance.now immediately before worker.postMessage until the matching response: includes structured clone, queue, raw-source guest bridge, compiler execution, and response. Worker boot excluded from edit timing. Fresh first check includes lazy imported-module checking; warm check and compile reuse the same worker/environment. Hover follows each changed check and is timed separately.
imported.hostConditions: Coordinated quiet window; see independent processes.jsonl and final qualification, not assumed idle.

fixture.source:
local json = require("nupp.codec.json")
local hex = require("nupp.codec.hex")
local text = require("nupp.text")
local utf8 = require("nupp.text.utf8")
local path = require("nupp.io.path")
local uri = require("nupp.io.uri")

local type Player = {
    name: string,
    score: integer,
    connected: boolean
}
local type Snapshot = {
    round: integer,
    names: {string},
    total: integer,
    payload: string
}

local function scorePlayers(players: {Player}, round: integer): Snapshot
    local names: {string} = {}
    local total: integer = 0
    for _, player in ipairs(players) do
        if player.connected then
            names[#names + 1] = utf8.truncate(player.name, 24)
            total = total + player.score
        end
    end
    table.sort(names)
    local payload = json.encode({round = round, players = names, total = total})

    return {round = round, names = names, total = total, payload = payload}
end

local function describe(snapshot: Snapshot): string
    local out = text.newBuffer()
    out:put("round=", tostring(snapshot.round), "\n")
    out:put("players=", table.concat(snapshot.names, ", "), "\n")
    out:put("total=", tostring(snapshot.total), "\n")
    out:put("payload=", hex.encode(snapshot.payload), "\n")

    return out:get()
end

local function destination(round: integer): (string, string)
    local localFile = path.newPath("scores", "round-" .. tostring(round)):withExtension("json")
    local endpoint = assert(uri.newURI("https://game.example/scores/"))
    local remoteFile = assert(endpoint:resolve(assert(localFile:fileName())))
    return localFile:toString(), remoteFile:toString()
end

local players: {
    Player
} = {
    {name = "Ada", score = 120, connected = true},
    {name = "Lin", score = 90, connected = true},
    {name = "Grace", score = 140, connected = false},
}
local round: integer = 5
local snapshot = scorePlayers(players, round)
local localFile, remoteFile = destination(round)
local report = describe(snapshot)
local wire = hex.encode("scoreboard-edit-5")
assert(hex.decode(wire) == "scoreboard-edit-5")
assert(snapshot.total == 210)
assert(utf8.length(snapshot.names[1]) == 3)
return report, localFile, remoteFile, wire

imported.edits: Replace round integer 5 and both scoreboard-edit-5 string literals with trial+5 on every request. Each compile must contain its current changed string. Every check/compile must return zero errors; every hover must identify wire as string. After timing, each imported API must reject a wrong argument with NUPP2006.
